rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 117, Line 11: "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 ... Figure this amount separately for you and your spouse", and p. 14, Married Filing Separately. The reply does not validate: its helpers s3.h_line3 and s3.h_line7 read s1.zero as a parameter; s1.zero is a Schedule 1 line, not a parameter ("s3.s3.h_line3: parameter 's1.zero' does not exist"; same for h_line7), so triage/s3.deepseek.json (executable-triage-v2) executed no line (6 x candidate invalid). The failure is in two helpers that only line 8 reads; it is not evidence about the other lines, which are ruled by reading against the source. The candidate sums person.credit as the project does, with a filter that keeps every person unless the return is married filing separately, when it keeps only the taxpayer. On every other return the filter is true for all persons and the lines agree; a married filing separately return is refused on this line by the project's cited s3.mfs screen. Not a model error: its earlier g28.line7 reading (round 1) is gone. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 117, Line 11: "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 and total wages of more than $176,100, too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld. You can take a credit on this line for the amount withheld in excess of $10,918.20 ... Figure this amount separately for you and your spouse." The candidate enters g28.line7, line 7 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet (collectibles gain), which has nothing to do with withheld social security tax; the project sums person.credit, the excess figured per person. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/s3.deepseek.json): 1,196 of 1,743 agree; 122 value differences (classm.f4562.1: project $10,917.80 against $0.00; classm.f5695.2: $1,677.80 against $0.00; classm.f8889.1.deepseek: $0.00 against $823.00 of 28% gain); 112 candidate-refuses and 17 candidate-unknown come from the Schedule D and dividend screens the worksheet reads (classm.dcprov.1: div.bad_components; classm.f8889.5.deepseek: sd.carryover; ss.multi: div.box2c unanswered, project $1,481.80); 201 project-refuses are the project's cited gates (person.rrta, the RRTA path; person.over, one employer over-withholding, Form 843; s3.mfs) and 95 project-unknown are older fixtures without person.rrta (table.band.first, switch.below), which every interview asks. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on the validation failure, not the tax reading. f1040s3 line 8, "Add lines 1 through 4, 5a, 5b, and 7". The candidate adds two helpers for lines 3 and 7 that read s1.zero as a parameter (it is a Schedule 1 line, and no such parameter exists); that is the reply's only validation error, and it is why triage executed nothing. In substance the sum equals the project's: lines 3 and 6a to 6z (so line 7) are refused through scope.credits, which both sides list on this line, so the added zeros change nothing on a computed return. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; f1040s3 (2025) p.1 line8 adds the nonrefundable credits. The compared project operands are NonNegDollars inputs or nonnegative credit computations. Subtracting constant zero with a floor therefore preserves their sum on every supported completed return. The formerly undefined zero parameters are absent from the final expanded line8 tree; the raw response remains preserved.
